title: Flash Sale Cart Reservation PostgreSQL Transaction Deadlock
businessContext: During a flash sale, shoppers simultaneously checkout carts containing multiple shared items (e.g. Shoes + Socks). Under peak concurrency, PostgreSQL logs show surging `ERROR: deadlock detected (SQLSTATE 40P01)`, causing 15% of checkout transactions to fail and abort.
problemStatement: When two concurrent checkout transactions attempt to lock the same inventory rows in different orders (Transaction A locks Product #101 then Product #205; Transaction B locks Product #205 then Product #101), neither transaction can proceed, causing a cyclical deadlock. Refactor the reservation logic to guarantee deterministic lock ordering.
constraints: Must maintain strict inventory consistency (no overselling beyond available stock).
Use deterministic sorting by Primary Key before locking (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`).
candidateTasks: Analyze PostgreSQL deadlock error logs and explain the Coffman conditions required for deadlocks.
Enforce deterministic lock acquisition ordering by sorting item IDs before executing `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`.
Discuss alternative lock acquisition methods like `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE NOWAIT` or `SKIP LOCKED`.
hints: If all concurrent transactions always acquire locks in the exact same global order (e.g. sorted ascending by `product_id`), a circular dependency cannot form.
You can sort `itemsToReserve.sort((a, b) => a.productId - b.productId)` before the loop or execute a single query: `SELECT ... WHERE product_id IN (...) ORDER BY product_id FOR UPDATE`.

testCases.name: Enforces deterministic primary key lock ordering
testCases.explanation: Guarantees deadlocks cannot occur across concurrent reservations.

alternativeApproaches: Single SQL statement batch update: UPDATE inventory SET stock = stock - updates.qty FROM ...
Using Redis distributed locks with Redlock algorithm ordered by key.
commonMistakes: Relying solely on retry logic: retries without ordering can cause repeated lock thrashing under high concurrency.
Using `SELECT ... FOR SHARE` which permits read sharing but escalates to exclusive write locks, actually increasing deadlocks.
